notes: Lead: VP Product (Maya Lin) contacted via community event (Nov 2025). Interested in faster time-to-market for in-product assistants and intelligent search.
Initial ask: replace current hybrid search+rules system w/ LLM-enabled reranking + doc-search. Also pilot internal code-assistant for engineers.
Evaluation path agreed: small Hosted API POC (2 weeks) -> performance + quality -> 6mo Dedicated POC if perf/cost targets met.
Hosted API demo (2026-02-22) w/ Alex: showed streaming chat, embeddings, and reranking pipeline. Team liked streaming + function calling for structured responses.
Cost optimization workshop (2026-02-15) with SE team (Priya): ran through batching profiles, prefix/KV caching, and quantization tradeoffs. Shared unit-economics template.

Workshop outcomes: recommended batching window 12-25ms for async routes, aggressive prefix cache for knowledge-intensive queries, evaluate int8 quantization for the 70% of calls that do not need full fidelity.
Quote from lead ML eng: 'If we can get effective token cost down to ~0.0008 per token-equivalent, this scales to product pricing targets.' — flagged as pricing hurdle.
Security: provided SOC2 attestation; customer requires SSO/SAML + audit logs and KMS integration before Dedicated kickoff. Security questionnaire 80% complete; infra team to answer network egress Qs.

Performance targets specified by customer: 95th pct latency <= 120ms for short-chat flows (<=128 tokens), bulk reranking throughput 200 reqs/s with steady tail latencies; embedding pipeline latency less strict (500ms).

Model preferences: prefer open models first (cost/benchmarks) but want Redwood-verified latency + fallback to smaller quantized variants. Routing policy: latency-first for front-end chat, cost-first for background reranking.
POC scope: 6-week hosted -> dedicated migration plan: 2 weeks hosted integration + eval, 2 weeks cost-optimization tuning (batching/caching/quant), 2 weeks smoke and SLA run for Dedicated sizing.
Internal stakeholder map: Maya Lin (VP Product), Owen Price (Director Eng), Priya Kapoor (SE), Lila Gomez (Procurement), Diego Ramos (Security).
Procurement notes: needs SOW + SAML ATO template. Pricing ask: reduction tiers at commit levels and optional burst capacity clauses.
Support artifacts: uploaded unit-econ spreadsheet (drive link), demo recordings in Fireflies id ff_20260303_bridgepoint-demo.
AE notes: keep pressure on hosted metrics; use cost-optimization workshop outputs to justify Dedicated commit. Emphasize rollback/fallback and identical API across Hosted/Dedicated.
Customer mental model: wants 'bring your model' later but initial comfort w/ Redwood-curated open models + quantized variants. Air-gap not needed at this stage.
Next internal ask from customer: a short runbook on KV cache invalidation patterns and expected cache hit rate assumptions for product KBs.

use_case_summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS product team wants to add LLM-based reranking and support/code-assistant. Starting on Hosted API to validate quality, then move to Dedicated for predictable costs and isolation. Focus of evaluation is unit economics: batching, caching, quantization profiles and routing policies to hit cost and latency targets.
customer_constraints: No air-gapped requirement. Must pass SOC2/security questionnaire and support SAML SSO + KMS. VPC peering for dedicated endpoints preferred. Procurement requires clear committed spend tiers and burst options.
sales_play_notes: Position: start w/ Hosted (fast integration) -> run cost-optimization workshop -> show delta to Dedicated pricing. Use unit economics template to demonstrate ROI. Offer a 6mo POC with commit credit toward Dedicated if accepted.
deal_risks: Security questionnaire answers delayed; procurement pushback on commit levels; If cost-per-token can't meet customer target, they'll consider self-host or larger cloud vendor discounts.
final_comments: High technical fluency on customer side — good SE-led conversations. Workshop helped align expectations; next 2 weeks are critical to lock security + pricing before procurement windows.
